title: Yet many acts not evil are left to free option, and are predefined only respectively, with regard to the will's determination
source_text: X. Veruntamen ut putat voluntatem hominum ad multos actus etiam ex se non malos, absolute a Deo in tempore non praedeterminari, sed liberam ipsi optionem permitti, ex duobus aut pluribus, quae utraque aut omnia sunt licita; sic etiam non putat omnes voluntatis actus, etiam qui peccati rationem non habent, fuisse absolute a Deo praedefinitos in aeternis ipsius decretis: sed, ut loquitur, respective solum; quia scilicet, praedefiniti non sunt ante & citra considerationem determinationis voluntatis creatae, sed cum respectu ad eam.
pass_a_gloss: X. Nevertheless as he thinks the will of men to many acts even not evil of themselves, is not absolutely predetermined by God in time, but free option is permitted to it, out of two or more, which both or all are lawful; so also he does not think that all acts of the will, even those which have not the nature of sin, were absolutely predefined by God in his eternal decrees: but, as he speaks, respectively only; because namely, they were not predefined before and apart from the consideration of the determination of the created will, but with respect to it.
pass_b_english: Even so, he thinks that for many acts which are not evil in themselves, men's wills are not absolutely predetermined by God in time; they are left a free option between two or more alternatives, all of them lawful.

Likewise he does not think that all acts of the will, even those without the character of sin, were absolutely predefined by God in his eternal decrees. They were predefined, in his phrase, only 'respectively': not before and apart from considering how the created will would determine itself, but with regard to that determination.

lemmas.gloss: free option is permitted to it

lemmas.latin: ante & citra considerationem determinationis voluntatis creatae
lemmas.gloss: before and apart from the consideration of the determination of the created will

choices.why: Strang's term for acts decreed with regard to the will's foreseen free choice, as opposed to 'absolutely'; kept as his technical adverb.
